newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee weakens on dollar and pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee weakens on dollar and pound.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee weakened against the dollar and the pound on Friday, following trends in international markets, commercial banks forex dealers said.
The rupee softened to a mean rate of 19.9715 against the dollar from 19.9555 on Thursday. Against the pound, the rupee was fixed at a mean rate of 33.6925 from 33.5530 on Thursday.
Forex dealers said the rupee's fixing reflected the dollar's trend in overnight international markets.

"Foreign exchange reserves in (commercial) banks are now square after the regular market interventions during the week. The levels of supply from the interventions were sufficient to meet demand for the time being," one dealer said.
The central bank was seen selling dollars in the interbank forex market during interventions on Monday and Tuesday.
Dealers said the intervention rates were below prevailing interbank rates and this contributed in supporting the rupee's value against the U.S. currency at the start of the week.
More hard currency supply to banks was made over the week by the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate with auction sales of pounds obtained from the island's sugar exports.
The syndicate held its tenders on Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
